title: Known plates are not getting recorded
body:
I must be doing something wrong because I seem to be the only one facing this issue. Known plates are not being processed or registered in my setup, and all of them are missing from new detections. If I add a new plate to the known plates, past occurrences are updated in the live feed with the correct name and notes. However, when any already-known plates drive through, they are not getting registered.

I tried debugging this but made no progress. Initially, I suspected that my database might have been corrupted during the update migrations, so I performed a fresh, clean installation. Unfortunately, the issue persists.

What could I be doing wrong?
author: olympia

comments.body: Is it still saying that the column does not exist?
No, it doesn't. And If I check with pgadmin, I see the column is there and all populated with 'false' for all records.

e6cc4ad74d5dc0771a51a12f55da17bad571fba4

You aren't the only one. Nobody else noticed. I stepped away for multiple days a few different times while making the changes for the last update. Makes it hard to resume and remember where exactly I was in the process. Seems like I broke a number of things in the process. Hopefully all fixed soon.

New image with that commit is building now. Should be ready in 5-10 minutes.

---

Seems like my gitignore is not working correctly also...

Thank you for checking and resolving the issue. Now that we know it affected everyone, I'm also surprised that no one else noticed it... :)

I've already updated it, but I'll only be able to confirm (if necessary) tomorrow when the traffic starts flowing.

Tomorrow, I might also try restoring my old database to avoid losing the two months of data it holds... :)

Thanks again!
I think postgres/pgadmin has something built in that should let you do the restoration
The fix works perfectly! Thank you!

title: Cannot remove plates from Known Plates Dashboard
body:
Running on Linux Docker with the latest repo changes.

Tested in both Chrome and Safari.

Clicking on the delete button within the table of known plates doesn't delete the plate.

Console Log:

```Failed to remove from known plates: ReferenceError: removeFromKnownPlates is not defined```
author: TinyShark

comments.body:
Thank you. Fix pushed. 

`docker compose down`, then `docker compose up -d` should fix. If not, `docker pull algertc/alpr-dashboard` and that should pull the latest version.

pulling the new image got it to work. Known plates are being removed correctly now.

Many thanks!
